observation.visible_scene: A yellow-and-black diagonally striped cylindrical press head is suspended in front of a pale textured wall, above a matching striped cylindrical base. A mound of green, blue and red-swirled glass marbles rests on the top face of the base. The caption text 'Glass Ball' is overlaid on the left at the start.
visible_changes: From t=0 the press head descends steadily, the vertical gap above the marble pile shrinking frame by frame while the marbles themselves remain piled and undisturbed.
The 'Glass Ball' overlay fades out around t=0.8–1.0.
Around t=1.4–1.8 the press head reaches the top of the pile and begins to bear on it; the multi-layered mound is progressively flattened into a thin single disc between the two striped surfaces.
As compression continues (t≈2.3 onward) the press head's mounting plate becomes visible at the top of the frame, consistent with the whole assembly moving downward while the base stays put.

From t≈2.33 to the end, marbles are squeezed radially out of the gap: blurred marbles streak off to the left and right and some drop over the front edge of the base, while the central layer stays compressed under the head.
The base cylinder and the wall background keep a fixed position and size throughout, indicating the apparent motion is the press descending rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The state before t=0 (when the press started descending) and the outcome after t=2.67 (full ejection, retraction of the head, or any shattering) are not shown.
Whether the press is powered or held by an unseen operator is not visible.
uncertain_details: Exact frame of first contact between head and marbles is approximate.
It is unclear whether any marbles fracture or only get pushed out; the moving marbles appear intact but heavily motion-blurred.
Camera motion cannot be fully ruled out, though background and base positions suggest the view is essentially static.
